editorial:
You follow thirteen-year-old Sam, a kid growing up in a rough city where crime keeps getting worse. He becomes convinced that his quiet neighbor Mr. Smith is actually Samaritan, the legendary vigilante everyone thought died twenty-five years ago. Sam's world is full of gangs, broken streets, and people who have given up, so his belief in a hero feels refreshing and real. The vibe feels like a gritty comic book story mixed with a coming-of-age tale, and it is easy to get pulled in by Sam's excitement and hope.

Sylvester Stallone brings real charm to Mr. Smith, and the action scenes are solid and fun to watch. The pacing moves quickly enough to keep you entertained, and the bond between Sam and Mr. Smith gives the movie its emotional core. The story has heart, but it can feel predictable at times, and some of the effects look a little rough. If you enjoy superhero stories with a darker edge, this one is worth your time.
endingExplained: In the final showdown, Mr. Smith battles the gang leader Cyrus and defeats him. Sam then learns the shocking truth: Mr. Smith is not Samaritan at all, but Nemesis, Samaritan's twin brother and rival. Samaritan actually died twenty-five years ago during their last fight. Nemesis has been living quietly ever since. Badly injured, Smith walks away, and the movie ends with Sam spotting a mysterious figure in the distance, hinting that the real Samaritan might still be alive.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves superhero stories with a darker edge.
